lines.text: Benchmarking Global Prosperity. Compare countries on food, poverty, health and education, and check every number against its source.
Pick a country. Kenya's profile opens with eighteen indicators from the U.N. System Data Commons, each with its latest value, its year, and its trend since twenty fifteen.
At the top, plain findings. On the left, the country on its own: what improved, what worsened, and where data is missing. On the right, how it compares with the countries or regions you choose.
Add a comparator. A country, a U.N. region, or a custom group you build yourself.
The Baseline view sets every indicator against the median country. There is no overall score, and no league table.
Compare shows the gap in bars, and where the country sits among all countries.
Trend shows change over time, against the twenty fifteen baseline and the S.D.G. target.
The map is a globe. Drag it, click a country, and India appears with its full boundary, including Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar islands.
Every value can be checked. This table shows the value in the platform, the official current value, the reporting agency, and a link to the source.
Some official values are thresholds, not measurements. Undernourishment below two point five percent is shown that way, and never used to compute a gap.
We compared all forty-eight thousand observations with the official publisher. Ninety-four percent are identical, and every difference is shown.
It works in the six U.N. languages, including Arabic, in light and dark.
Benchmarking Global Prosperity. From data to insight, evidence and progress.
